This PR adds mappings for OpenTelemetry data via a new plugin `otel-data`

The PR is mainly based on:
- the existing apm-data plugin from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97546
- the https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455 draft PR by @felixbarny - most of the mappings are from there

- Created `YamlTemplateRegistry` as an abstract base class that loads mappings from YAML. The code of this class comes from `APMIndexTemplateRegistry` which now derives from `YamlTemplateRegistry`. The shared code is now moved to `core`.
- Added `otel-data` plugin with `OtelIndexTemplateRegistry` which also derives from `YamlTemplateRegistry`.
- Moved the mappings into YAML files from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455.

Because ES|QL doesn't support `date_nanos` at the moment (see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/109352), I think we need to revert to using `date` for now, until ES|QL reaches an acceptable level of support for `date_nanos`.

@mlunadia @strawgate @tylerperk, we could use your help to define what acceptable means and what level of parity we need in order for us to be ready to use the `date_nanos` field type. Do we need the experience with `date_nanos` to not be worse in any aspects compared to `date`? Are we willing to make compromises, for example users having to make manual casts in ES|QL? What are the essentials and what are the nice to haves?

reply.body: Would it make sense to default to `date` here but override it to `date_nanos` for specific datasets? I think most integrations do not use `date_nanos` today and it carries with it perf/storage costs?

They don't but we're also discussing changing this as a default for integrations: https://github.com/elastic/logs-dev/issues/25

There's minimal overhead if `date_nanos` is used as a field type but the timestamps are only in ms precision. As OTel timestamps are defined in [nanosecond in OTLP](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto/blob/484241a016d7b81f20b6e19d00ffbc4a3b864a22/opentelemetry/proto/logs/v1/logs.proto#L140), I think we should also map them this way, without losing precision, by choosing the `date_nanos` field type by default.

Users can still override this and chose `date` instead.

However, in the short term, because of the limitations in ES|QL, I don't think we can use the `date_nanos` field type, yet.

> Tried to push a metrics-otel@custom mapping - I was not able to figure out how to do that with this yml syntax. 

When you search for `cluster.put_component_template`, you can find a bunch of examples.

It should be something similar to 

```yml
  - do:
      cluster.put_component_template:
        name: metrics-otel@custom
        body:
          template:
            settings:
              index:
                time_series:
                  start_time: 2024-07-01T13:03:08.138Z
```

If setting the start_time doesn't work here, I have another idea which involves setting the `@timestamp` in an ingest pipeline.

```yml
  - do:
      ingest.put_pipeline:
        id: "default_timestamp"
        body:  >
          {
            "description": "_description",
            "processors": [
              {
                "set": {
                  "description": "If '@timestamp' is missing, set it with the ingest timestamp",
                  "field": "@timestamp",
                  "override": false,
                  "copy_from": "_ingest.timestamp"
                }
              }
            ]
          }
  - match: { acknowledged: true }

  - do:
      cluster.put_component_template:
        name: metrics-otel@custom
        body:
          template:
            settings:
              index:
                default_pipeline: default_timestamp
```

+## OpenTelemetry Ingest plugin
+
+The OpenTelemetry Ingest plugin installs index templates and component templates for Elastic OpenTelemetry data.
+
+All resources are defined as YAML under [src/main/resources](src/main/resources).
+
+The OpenTelemetry index templates rely on mappings from `x-pack-core`.

+
+All resources are defined as YAML under [src/main/resources](src/main/resources).
+
+For a resource to be known to the plugin it must be added to
+[src/main/resources/resources.yaml](src/main/resources/resources.yaml) in the
+appropriate section.
+
+Any update to resources included by this package also requires a bump to the

+
